# ModulusLift — a check passed at one cycle carries up to every multiple of it

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

A list of speeds is good at a denominator when some time with that denominator is lonely. A good time with one denominator is also good with any multiple of it (stretch the numerator by the same factor), and whether a list is good depends only on the speeds' remainders. So a list whose remainders were good at a smaller cycle never needs checking at a larger cycle built on it (bad_lists_lift); a list whose all-but-one share a factor with the smaller cycle still shares it with the larger one (proper_lifts). This is the same climb as rotating one more wheel into the combined cycle. Trakulthongchai 2026, Definition 6 and Lemma 7: the sieve on the modulus that took the record to nine and ten runners. Uses only the vocabulary of PileUpLock.

## Claims

<a id="far_scale"></a>
### `far_scale`

The point c times y of a lap cut into c times d parts is the same place as the point y of a lap cut into d parts.

```lean
/-- **Stretching the cycle.** The point `c * y` of a lap of `c * d` parts is the
same place as the point `y` of a lap of `d` parts. -/
def far_scale : Prop :=
  ∀ (n d c : ℕ) (y : ℤ), 0 < c → (far n (c * d) ((c : ℤ) * y) ↔ far n d y)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ModulusLift.far_scale_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean)

<a id="good_lifts"></a>
### `good_lifts`

A list good at a denominator is good at every multiple of it.

```lean
/-- **Good at a cycle, good at every multiple.** -/
def good_lifts : Prop :=
  ∀ (n d d' : ℕ) (R : Multiset ℤ), 0 < d' → d ∣ d' → good_at n d R → good_at n d' R
```

**Rests on:** [`ModulusLift.far_scale`](ModulusLift.md#far_scale)

**Proof:** `RNS.ModulusLift.good_lifts_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean)

<a id="good_residues"></a>
### `good_residues`

Whether a list is good at a denominator depends only on the speeds' remainders for it.

```lean
/-- **Only remainders matter for being good.** -/
def good_residues : Prop :=
  ∀ (n d : ℕ) (R : Multiset ℤ), good_at n d (R.map (fun r => r % (d : ℤ))) ↔ good_at n d R
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ModulusLift.good_residues_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean)

<a id="bad_lists_lift"></a>
### `bad_lists_lift`

If a list's remainders for a cycle are good, so are its remainders for every multiple of that cycle (Trakulthongchai's Lemma 7).

```lean
/-- **Bad lists at a larger cycle lie over bad lists at the smaller.** If the
remainders of a list for the cycle `d` are good, so are its remainders for any
multiple `d'` of `d`. -/
def bad_lists_lift : Prop :=
  ∀ (n d d' : ℕ) (R : Multiset ℤ), 0 < d' → d ∣ d' →
    good_at n d (R.map (fun r => r % (d : ℤ))) → good_at n d' (R.map (fun r => r % (d' : ℤ)))
```

**Rests on:** [`ModulusLift.good_lifts`](ModulusLift.md#good_lifts), [`ModulusLift.good_residues`](ModulusLift.md#good_residues)

**Proof:** `RNS.ModulusLift.bad_lists_lift_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean)

<a id="proper_lifts"></a>
### `proper_lifts`

A number sharing a factor with a cycle shares one with every multiple of the cycle.

```lean
/-- **A shared factor with the cycle carries up.** If a number shares a factor
with the cycle `d`, it shares one with every multiple of `d`. -/
def proper_lifts : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : ℤ) (d d' : ℕ), d ∣ d' → Int.gcd A d ≠ 1 → Int.gcd A d' ≠ 1
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ModulusLift.proper_lifts_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ModulusLift.lean)
